name: Hilda Solis

items.text: A 1999 state law, SB 63, lowered the El Monte Busway carpool rule from three riders to two starting January 1, 2000. A federal study found it slowed buses and brought about 900 rider complaints to Foothill Transit. The three-rider rule returned at peak hours on July 24, 2000.
items.why: This is an ordinary legislative policy that backfired and was corrected within months, with no abuse of office, self-dealing or false statement shown under criterion 6 or any other criterion.

for_review: I read the FHWA/Texas Transportation Institute case study (June 2002). It confirms the bill, the January 2000 change, the harm to the busway and the July 24, 2000 restoration of the 3+ peak rule through AB 769. It doesn't name Solis. Her authorship of SB 63, her first defense of the change and her co-sponsoring the repeal rest only on Wikipedia, which I didn't treat as proof. A reviewer could check the LA Times articles of Jan 22, 2000 and July 27, 2000, and the bill's legislative history, for her own words. The search on the owner's named sites (alexjoneslive.com, stewpeters.com, ryandawson.org, infowars.com) returned nothing relevant to Solis. I searched only once and did not check each site's own pages.
